M1.reason: The outline is a flat slab, about 32.4 by 10.5 by 2 (sides.png). The FRONT and BACK views show a low sliver, and the LEFT and RIGHT views a straight bar with no bend. The brief asks for a bar with a hooked claw at one end, and no view of any of the ten shows a claw, hook or shaft.

M2.reason: Length is 32.4 against the brief's 32, 1.3% off, inside 15%. The brief gives only a length, so width and height have no target to check against.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for: a shaft, a hooked claw at one end, a flattened tip at the other. The asset has a flat wedge at one end (FRONT-LEFT, BACK-RIGHT) and no claw or hook anywhere, and no round shaft. The claw is missing, so M3 is at most 1 and the claw's absence makes it 0.

M4.reason: The brief asks for red paint on the shaft and bare metal at the tips. Every view of the asset (sides.png, attack.png, first-person.png left) is a uniform grey with no red anywhere. Against the game's red crowbar on first-person.png right, the difference is far over 15.

M5.reason: A faint diagonal streak and lighter bevelled edges at the ends (sides.png TOP, lineup D) suggest some wear. But the red paint is absent, and the tips do not read as worn to bare metal in any view.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. The line-up test was run four times with the asset at D, B, C and B, and the judges picked C, B, D and A. Three of four readings passed it as one of the game's, so the measure does not catch it. By eye in lineup.png it is a plain grey plank beside the guns and the shell, which is why the other items score low. The M6 score rests on the measure, not on my view of the picture.

M7.reason: The brief gives no facing. The asset lies flat in its FRONT and BACK views (a low sliver) and has no upright front to read, so it does not stand as a crowbar does. It stands on its origin, but as a plank, not as a bar held in the hand.

M8.reason: The SMAK check has no errors (checkErrors empty). It has 10 triangles against a budget far above that. The solid reads closed from every side in sides.png, with the dark wedge faces the shading of a slanted face, not an opening. Nothing is seen floating.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits at the left of the frame at a steep tilt, while the game's own crowbar sits at the right with its claw up in the view. The asset is not held where the original sits or the same way round. In attack.png the slab moves through the frames: frame 3/10 has a dark shape at its base, and the weapon leaves the picture rather than parting from a hand. Position and grip are clearly off, so the item is there but wrong.
